title: Grid orchestration: phased cell-measure cache, keyboard-first column shims, and adaptive density snapshots
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Large, heterogeneous tables in our apps show janky resize behavior, header layout jumps during initial scroll, and poor keyboard affordances for column reflow. Current virtualized table measures cells synchronously on first paint and invalidates layouts too aggressively when density or font scales change. Goals: (1) reduce visual jank on first interaction for datasets >10k rows; (2) provide keyboard-first column-resize and reorder 'shims' that feel native to power users; (3) introduce an immutable short-lived cell-measure cache to avoid repeated layout thrash when switching density modes or sorting; (4) keep accessibility and screen-reader announcements clear during progressive measurements and density transitions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) On a 100k synthetic row dataset, initial vertical scroll to row 500 should not trigger more than two reflows within the first 2s on a mid-range laptop. 2) Keyboard-resize mode: users can Tab into header, press Space to enter resize shim, use Arrow keys to adjust width (by 8px) and get a live preview; Escape cancels and Enter persists. 3) Density snapshot: switching between Compact/Cozy/Comfort stores a short-lived snapshot that applies immediately to visible viewport; subsequent full reflow must be deferred and run off-main where possible. 4) Automated tests for resize keyboard interactions, density-change visual regressions, and a perf harness measure are added to the design verification checklist.
design_notes: - Introduce a Phased Cell-Measure Cache: stage 0 = quick heuristics (row height estimate from token count + font-scale); stage 1 = async precise measurement for viewport; stage 2 = full-viewport stabilization run when idle. Cache keys include column schema hash + density token + user-font-scale. Cache TTL is short (30s) and cleared on structural changes (column add/remove).
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Pro: dramatically lowers first-interaction jank and reduces GC pressure from repeated DOM reads. Con: adds complexity to invalidation logic; risk of stale measurements if custom cell renderers compute variable heights after async measurement — mitigation: provide an API for renderers to opt into "post-measure" invalidation. - Keyboard shims add a small cognitive overhead but improve discoverability for accessibility-focused keyboard users.
implementation_outline: 1) Design tokens: add density snapshot token group (densitySnapshotId) and expose API in Table props. 2) Runtime: implement cache layer in row-measure service (ENG to own low-level implementation). 3) UX: header shim component — visible only in keyboard mode, visually distinct from pointer handles, with microcopy tooltip. 4) QA: perf harness and Storybook stories: large-data scenarios, density toggle, keyboard-only interactions. 5) Rollout: feature-flag gated; experiment on 5% of internal users then ramp.
accessibility: - Keyboard shim will follow ARIA roletype of 'separator' with aria-orientation and live region announcements when width changes. - Use polite live region for progress of async measurement ('Table layout stabilizing') and assert that screen readers do not receive repeated noisy announcements. - Ensure focus is not lost during async reflows; focus trap in header-resize mode until exit.
performance_budget: Target: TTFP layout stabilization within 1.2s for 95th percentile on internal perf lab (MacBook Pro 2018 equivalent). Memory: incremental measurement should not retain more than 3x the average cell size per visible viewport. Telemetry: emit events for measurement stages and cache hits/misses.
rollout_plan: - Phase A: internal dogfood across Console QA team behind feature flag. - Phase B: enable for 5% of production requests on hosted-apps with large-table telemetry; monitor reflow counts and accessibility errors. - Phase C: full release and documentation update in component library. Provide migration guide for teams with custom cell renderers.
testing_notes: - Add unit tests for cache key generation and TTL behavior. - Add e2e Puppeteer script to emulate keyboard-resize flows and measure reflow counts. - Visual tests: Percy stories for density transitions and header shim states. - Accessibility tests: Axe run in CI and manual SR inspection for NVDA/VoiceOver.
